This application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking pre- arrest bail.

2. The applicant is the accused in Crime No.681/2025 of Sreekariyam Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram District.

The offences alleged are punishable under Section 4(1) read with Section 3(a), Section 6 read with Section 5(l)(m)(n) and Section 12 read with Section 11(i) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012; Section 376, 376(2)(n), 376(2)(f), 376 AB of the Indian Penal Code and Section 75 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,
2015.

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case, in short, is that the applicant committed rape on the victim four times while she was studying in 6th standard and thereby committed the aforementioned offences.
4. I have heard Smt.Anupama Subramanian, the learned counsel for the applicant and Sri.K.A.Noushad, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Notice has been served to the defacto 2026:KER:20484 BAIL APPL. NO. 896 OF 2026 complainant.
She is not present or represented by counsel.
However, she has filed a statement through the learned Senior Public Prosecutor stating that she strongly opposes the bail application.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the above crime.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicant's intentional criminal acts, and if he is released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
6. The applicant is the first cousin of the victim.
Going by the FIR and FIS, the incident took place in the year 2019.
The FIR was registered in the year 2025.
At the time of the alleged incident, the victim was residing at the house of the applicant.
At that time, the victim was aged 12 years and the applicant was aged 17 years.
In short, the applicant was a juvenile at the time of the incident.

It is true that there is a bar under Section 482(4) of the BNSS (Section 438(4) of Cr.P.C.) in granting pre-arrest bail 2026:KER:20484 BAIL APPL. NO. 896 OF 2026 to an accused involved in the offence of rape of a girl below 12 years.

However, this Court in XXX v. State of Kerala [2023 (6) KHC 158] has held that Section 438(4) of Cr.P.C does not create an absolute bar in granting pre-arrest bail to an accused involved in the offence of rape of a minor girl.

entities.text: XXX v. State of Kerala [2023 (6) KHC 158]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further held that when no case is made out or allegations are patently false or motivated, the bar under Section 438(4) of Cr.P.C. will not apply and the court can still grant pre-arrest bail.
7.
As stated already, the applicant and the victim were close relatives and at the time of the alleged incident, they were residing at the house of the applicant.
Both of them were minors.
It appears that there developed a teen romance between them.
The undue delay of six years in lodging the FIR has not been reasonably explained.
I went through the FIS as well as the statement given by the victim under Section 183 of the BNSS.
There are inconsistencies and contradictions in both versions.

That apart, Annexure B would show that another FIR has been registered against the father of the Nivash vs State Of Kerala on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41013231/
2 applicant.
In the FIS given by the victim in the said crime, there is a reference to the sexual assault made by the applicant as well.
But absolutely no details 2026:KER:20484 BAIL APPL. NO. 896 OF 2026 have been mentioned.
Considering all these aspects, I am of the view that this is a case where the bar under Section 482(4) of the BNSS is attracted and the applicant can be granted pre-arrest bail.
8. It is reported that the applicant is at present abroad.

The applicant should be directed to come back to India and co- operate with the investigation within a stipulated time limit as held by the Division Bench of this Court in Anu Mathew v. State of Kerala [2023 (3) KHC 151].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the allegations made against the applicant, his custodial interrogation seems unnecessary.
For these reasons, I find this to be an appropriate case to grant pre-arrest bail to the applicant.

In the result, the application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall come back to India within a period of three weeks from today and co-operate with the investigation.
(ii) The applicant shall be released on bail in the event of his arrest on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the arresting officer/investigating officer, as the 2026:KER:20484 BAIL APPL. NO. 896 OF 2026 case may be.
(iii) The applicant shall subject himself to the deemed police custody for discovery, if any, as and when demanded.
(iv) The applicant shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m.
and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
He shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
(v) The applicant shall not commit any offence of a like nature while on bail.

(vi) The applicant shall not attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses,
directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
(vii) The applicant shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.
(viii) The application, if any, for deletion/modification of bail conditions or cancellation of bail on the grounds of violating the bail conditions shall be filed at the jurisdictional court.

(ix) If the applicant fails to comply with the direction of this Court to come back to India within three weeks from today, the 2026:KER:20484 BAIL APPL. NO. 896 OF Nivash vs State Of Kerala on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41013231/
3 2026 order granting pre-arrest bail to him shall stand vacated.
